fleetops_discovery_and_workflow.overview: This file defines the discovery phase and overall workflow for building FleetOps cold-chain logistics agents and tools. The mode follows a structured approach: Discovery → Planning → Implementation → Deployment → Documentation.

discovery_phase.purpose: Understand the user's requirements before building any agents or tools. Gather information about the logistics workflow, API endpoints, and integration needs.

question_group.name: project_context
question_group.question: Are you working with an existing FleetOps project or starting fresh?
Do you have existing agents or tools that need modification?
What is the primary goal of this agent/tool? (e.g., weather analysis, routing, decision-making, notifications)

question_group.name: domain_understanding
question_group.question: What type of cargo or shipment does this involve? (e.g., pharmaceuticals, food, chemicals)
What are the critical temperature thresholds or constraints?
What triggers the need for this agent? (e.g., temperature alerts, route deviations, weather conditions)

question_group.name: technical_requirements
question_group.question: What is your FleetOps API base URL? (e.g., https://your-api.example.com or http://localhost:8085)
What backend APIs or services does this agent/tool need to integrate with?

question_group.name: input_output_schema
question_group.question: What data fields does the agent need to receive as input? Please describe each field with its type and purpose.
What data fields should the agent output? Please describe the complete output schema.
Are there any nested objects or arrays in the input/output? Please describe their structure.
What are the data types for each field? (string, integer, float, boolean, array, object)

question_group.name: workflow_integration
question_group.question: Where does this agent fit in the overall workflow? (beginning, middle, end)
What agent should run before this one?
What agent should run after this one?
How should errors be handled? (retry, fallback, abort)

discovery_best_practices.practice: ALWAYS ask for the FleetOps API URL first - never use hardcoded URLs
Ask 2-3 questions at a time to avoid overwhelming the user
Use follow-up questions to clarify ambiguous answers
Analyze existing codebase (agents/, tools/) to understand patterns
Identify API endpoints by reading existing tool implementations
Document all gathered requirements including API URL before proceeding
Remind users to set FLEETOPS_API_URL environment variable or use credentials

phase.name: Discovery
phase.description: Gather requirements and understand the use case

actions.action: Ask discovery questions about the agent/tool purpose
Ask user to define input schema with field names, types, and descriptions
Ask user to define output schema with field names, types, and descriptions
Clarify any nested structures or complex data types
Analyze existing codebase if present (but don't assume schemas)
Document requirements clearly including complete schemas

completion_criteria.criterion: Input schema fully defined by user
Output schema fully defined by user

actions.action: Ask user if they want a plan.md file created
If yes, switch to Plan mode to create detailed plan
Include agent structure, tool design, API integration approach
Define Pydantic schemas based on user-provided input/output specifications
Map user's field descriptions to proper Pydantic Field definitions

completion_criteria.criterion: Pydantic schemas match user's specifications exactly

phase.name: Implementation
phase.description: Build the agent YAML and Python tools

actions.action: Create agent YAML file with proper structure
Write agent instructions with JSON output format matching user's schema
Define Pydantic models based on user-provided schemas (not existing patterns)
Ensure field names, types, and descriptions match user specifications
Add API integration code with error handling
Implement retry logic and fallback strategies

completion_criteria.criterion: Agent YAML is valid and complete
Pydantic models exactly match user-defined schemas
No assumptions made about data structure

actions.action: Ensure error handling covers edge cases

completion_criteria.criterion: Agent instructions are clear and complete

phase.name: Deployment
phase.description: Prepare for deployment to watsonx Orchestrate

codebase_analysis.when_to_analyze: Analyze the existing codebase when: - User mentions existing agents or tools - Modifying or extending existing functionality - Understanding integration patterns - Learning API endpoint structures

analyze_agents.action: Read existing agent YAML files in agents/ directory
Understand agent instructions and output formats

analyze_tools.action: Read Python tool files in tools/ directories

important_rules.rule: CRITICAL: Always ask users for their FleetOps API URL - NEVER hardcode production URLs
CRITICAL: Always ask users to define input/output schemas - NEVER assume or reuse existing schemas
Always start with discovery questions before implementation
Ask users to specify each field name, type, and description for inputs and outputs
Create Pydantic models based on user specifications, not existing patterns
Offer to create plan.md before coding
Analyze existing code to understand patterns but don't copy schemas
Get user approval at major decision points
Remind users to configure FLEETOPS_API_URL environment variable
